item.description: • The Anthropic API is an agent of its own in Settings › Agents, on a key from the Claude Console, billed to that key's organization and never to your Claude subscription. It runs in Claude Code with the key as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which outranks your Claude login, and no other Anthropic credential reaches it. Its threads have Claude Code's models, levels and fast mode where your organization has it, and show what each turn cost, but no plan usage or limits and no Continue in Terminal, where `claude` would run on your subscription. Its models are drawn under Anthropic's mark; Claude Code's keep Claude's. • ⌘K's Open a Claude Code session is Import sessions…: the project's sessions from Claude Code, Codex, T3 Code, OpenCode, Copilot and Cursor, each with its tool's name and its agent's mark, and Import all for every one that isn't a thread yet. A session comes in on the agent that ran it and goes on in the same session where that agent is on and can pick one up by its id, a T3 Code thread in the Claude, Codex or Cursor session under it. Cursor's chats, and a Claude Code session begun under another path to the folder, through a symlink, come in with their transcript, which your next message hands over to the agent a new thread starts on. Codex's and OpenCode's are listed only while those agents are on. Nothing is written into the other tools' files. • Auto and Don't ask do what they say on the agents besides Claude Code. On Codex, Auto has Codex's own reviewer judge each request's risk instead of asking you, and a project added through a symlink no longer fails every command in Codex's sandbox and asks to run it outside. On every agent that asks, Don't ask answers its asks for you, those already waiting included, and switching to it mid-turn works from that moment. Cursor and Antigravity have Don't ask now. OpenCode no longer offers Auto, which there was only your own OpenCode settings. • A pasted megabyte no longer freezes the window, as it was pasted, as it was sent, or every time its thread opened after. A message longer than 20,000 characters shows its first twelve lines, its size, Show more and Copy, which copies all of it; the agent still gets all of it. Codex takes up to 1,048,576 characters, and a longer message says so and stays in the message bar instead of going out to Codex's error. • Water, in Settings › Conversation, turns the usage glass left of Send into a glass of water on Claude Code's threads, and says nothing of the plan there. It fills with today's water against a usual day, the average of the 30 days before today, and brims past one. Its card is the water of the thread, today, this week and this month, every Claude Code session on this Mac counted once, and the rate and its source are under the pointer on "estimated". The thread's figure still ends its latest turn's footer. • The thread beside has a capsule of its own over its column, in the title capsule's glass, its cross at the right end where a tab's is, away from its working mark. A click there no longer looks like stopping it: the capsule draws itself into a drop, runs up to the window's capsule and flows into its end, and the thread you leave buds out of the other end as a drop, pinches off and falls into the other column's capsule. With Reduce Motion the titles only fade.
